chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Umar ibn Ali, from his uncle, from one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That a man came to him and complained to him of his need, and exaggerated in his complaint until he was on the verge of complaining of hunger. He said: So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'O man, do you pray at night?' He said: And the man said, 'Yes.' He said: So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) turned to his companions and said, 'He who claims that he prays at night and goes hungry by day is lying. Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, has guaranteed sustenance for the day through the prayer of the night.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual guarantee of night prayer regarding daily sustenance?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) corrects a man’s complaint of hunger by linking it to the sincerity of his night prayer (Qiyam al-Layl), asserting that Allah has guaranteed sustenance (rizq) for those who truly engage in it. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual efficacy of night worship as a means of securing divine provision, distinguishing between mere ritual performance and the spiritual reality that ensures sustenance.
